corrected_prompt:
Format: Handmade claymation stop-motion look: plasticine characters with visible thumbprints and slight tool marks, soft rounded forms, miniature handmade set pieces, warm practical lighting, shallow depth of field like a tabletop set, gentle stop-motion texture. Stop-motion clay puppet detail: tiny real craft materials on the clay, thread-wrapped hair, real fabric and felt, real stitching. Palette: warm ivory and marble, charcoal accents. A set reference sheet, vertical 9:16: the top 70% is one wide view of an empty miniature clay home office; the bottom 30% is a strip of three close panels side by side with thin ivory gutters.

Reference images: none attached.

Subject, top 70%: the room has no full-size people; the only figures are the 12 small clay clients in the organizer and the six tiny street figures outside the window. On the back wall, left of centre, spanning from 6% to 70% of the frame width and from 12% to 36% from the top, clear of the window: a felt wall organizer about 60 cm wide: ivory felt with charcoal stitching, a header band at the top with the word "CLIENTS" stitched in big charcoal capitals, exactly FOUR columns by TWO rows of open-topped pockets (eight pockets in all), the APRIL pockets aligned directly under the MARCH pockets, a thick label band at the left end of each row with "MARCH" on the upper row and "APRIL" on the lower row in big charcoal capitals. Each MARCH pocket holds three small clay client figures shown from the chest up above the pocket rim, smiling softly, in blazers of different colours (12 in all); all four APRIL pockets are empty, their openings showing dark brown-grey felt inside. Bottom strip, left to right: (1) the same laptop seen from the front, open; (2) the small round charcoal bin, empty; (3) a close view of the window with the six tiny figures.

Hands: no hands anywhere in the sheet; no full-size people (the only figures are the 12 small clay clients and the six tiny street figures).

Action: none, a still set sheet.

Props: in the wide view, below the organizer, a charcoal clay desk with an open silver laptop whose back faces the camera and whose screen faces the wall, a white mug, a small brass lamp, a charcoal headset, and a pile of papers with a big orange felt tag on top. On the right wall, from 76% to 97% of the frame width and 15% to 55% from the top, a window: outside, a clay street with six tiny clay figures standing on the pavement looking up; beside the window a thin wooden rod with small loops, nothing hanging on it. Close panel 1: the open silver clay laptop from the front, a narrow charcoal bezel and a plain softly glowing pale-blue blank screen with no icons, windows or words. Close panel 2: a small round charcoal clay waste bin with a thumb-pressed rim, empty inside. Close panel 3: the window and the six tiny figures looking up.

Text: exactly four strings in charcoal capitals: "CLIENTS" on the organizer's header band, top centre; "MARCH" on the upper row's label band at its left end; "APRIL" on the lower row's label band at its left end; "MARCH" on the orange felt tag on the paper pile, left of the laptop. Nothing covers any letter. No other lettering anywhere, and none on the laptop screen.

Setting: warm ivory marble-textured clay wall, warm wooden clay floor, morning light from the window. No posters, frames, book titles or signs.

Camera: the wide view from inside the miniature set at desk height; the desk sits between 40% and 68% from the top; the close panels straight-on; every element inside a 4% margin; vertical 9:16.

Continuity: the organizer is the locked CLIENTS organizer design described above, state A: March full, April empty.

Negatives: no full-size people, no Maya (the 12 small clay clients and six tiny street figures are required); no loose fabric scraps and no sand-cream cloth pieces; no clients in the APRIL pockets; nothing on the rod; no icons, apps or words on the laptop screen; no logos. Everything in frame is real modeling clay, felt and fabric, photographed: visible fingerprints and tool marks, real cast shadows, soft studio lighting.
